← debttoincomeratio.org home

Rhode Island Debt-to-Income Ratio [2026]: HFA Overlays, 43% QM Rule, and DTI Breaking Points

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Rhode Island residents.

Rhode Island Debt-to-Income Ratio (DTI) Reference

Debt-to-income ratio (DTI) is the single most-used number in Rhode Island mortgage, auto, and credit-card underwriting. It has two flavors:

Front-end DTI: Monthly housing cost (PITI) / gross monthly income. Mortgage lenders watch this for affordability.

Back-end DTI: Total monthly debt payments (PITI + auto + student + credit card minimums + alimony/child support) / gross monthly income. This is the big one.

ThresholdProgram / Rule

28% front-endConventional conservative benchmark; GSE "housing ratio" guideline.

36% back-end"28/36 rule" conservative benchmark.

43%Qualified Mortgage (QM) safe-harbor cap under 12 CFR 1026.43; FHA max generally 43-50% with compensating factors.

50%Conventional max with AUS approval (Fannie Mae DU / Freddie Mac LPA); USDA guaranteed cap.

57%VA max back-end DTI for borrowers with adequate residual income.

Rhode Island Median Income and DTI Reference Lines

Median household income in Rhode Island is approximately $81,400/year, or $6,783/month (ACS 2022).

28% front-end housing cap for median-income Rhode Island household: $1,899/month.

43% back-end cap (QM safe harbor): $2,916/month total debt payments.

Average Rhode Island credit card balance: $6,450. Minimum at 2% = $129/month; this alone consumes 1.9% of median monthly income.

This is why Rhode Island households with above-average credit card balances push rapidly into mortgage-disqualifying DTI, even without a car note.

Rhode Island state housing finance agencies (HFAs) have their own DTI overlays that may be more or less lenient than FHA/conventional. Current Rhode Island overlay:

RIHousing FirstHomes: 45% DTI; 660 min.

HFA programs pair generous DTI with down-payment assistance, so a Rhode Island household near 43-50% back-end DTI should check HFA options before assuming mortgage-unqualified status.

What to Do When Rhode Island DTI Is Above 50%

Back-end DTI above 50% means most conventional relief tools (refi, HELOC, consolidation loan) are closed off. Options by severity:

50-57%: VA-loan refi (if eligible); HFA assistance; nonprofit credit counseling DMP. Budget restructure.

57-65%: DMP aggressive; debt settlement selectively; Chapter 13 for auto cram-down or mortgage arrears (if applicable).

>65%: Bankruptcy territory. Means test to determine Ch 7 vs. Ch 13.

The "Means Test" Is Income-Based, Not DTI-Based

Important: the federal bankruptcy means test (11 U.S.C. 707(b)) screens on income (6-month average vs. Rhode Island median), not DTI. So a Rhode Island household with 80% DTI but below-median income still qualifies for Chapter 7; a below-median DTI with above-median income might be pushed into Chapter 13.

The Rhode Island median-income thresholds are updated semi-annually by the UST. See means test explainer.

## Vermont Debt-to-Income Ratio [2026]: HFA Overlays, 43% QM Rule, and DTI Breaking Points
Source: https://debttoincomeratio.org/states/vermont.html

← debttoincomeratio.org home

Vermont Debt-to-Income Ratio [2026]: HFA Overlays, 43% QM Rule, and DTI Breaking Points

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Vermont residents.

Vermont Debt-to-Income Ratio (DTI) Reference

Debt-to-income ratio (DTI) is the single most-used number in Vermont mortgage, auto, and credit-card underwriting. It has two flavors:

Front-end DTI: Monthly housing cost (PITI) / gross monthly income. Mortgage lenders watch this for affordability.

Back-end DTI: Total monthly debt payments (PITI + auto + student + credit card minimums + alimony/child support) / gross monthly income. This is the big one.

ThresholdProgram / Rule

28% front-endConventional conservative benchmark; GSE "housing ratio" guideline.

36% back-end"28/36 rule" conservative benchmark.

43%Qualified Mortgage (QM) safe-harbor cap under 12 CFR 1026.43; FHA max generally 43-50% with compensating factors.

50%Conventional max with AUS approval (Fannie Mae DU / Freddie Mac LPA); USDA guaranteed cap.

57%VA max back-end DTI for borrowers with adequate residual income.

Vermont Median Income and DTI Reference Lines

Median household income in Vermont is approximately $74,000/year, or $6,166/month (ACS 2022).

28% front-end housing cap for median-income Vermont household: $1,726/month.

43% back-end cap (QM safe harbor): $2,651/month total debt payments.

Average Vermont credit card balance: $5,800. Minimum at 2% = $116/month; this alone consumes 1.9% of median monthly income.

This is why Vermont households with above-average credit card balances push rapidly into mortgage-disqualifying DTI, even without a car note.

Vermont HFA / First-Time Homebuyer DTI Overlay

Vermont state housing finance agencies (HFAs) have their own DTI overlays that may be more or less lenient than FHA/conventional. Current Vermont overlay:

VHFA Move: 45% DTI; 640 min.

HFA programs pair generous DTI with down-payment assistance, so a Vermont household near 43-50% back-end DTI should check HFA options before assuming mortgage-unqualified status.

What to Do When Vermont DTI Is Above 50%

Back-end DTI above 50% means most conventional relief tools (refi, HELOC, consolidation loan) are closed off. Options by severity:

50-57%: VA-loan refi (if eligible); HFA assistance; nonprofit credit counseling DMP. Budget restructure.

57-65%: DMP aggressive; debt settlement selectively; Chapter 13 for auto cram-down or mortgage arrears (if applicable).

>65%: Bankruptcy territory. Means test to determine Ch 7 vs. Ch 13.

The "Means Test" Is Income-Based, Not DTI-Based

Important: the federal bankruptcy means test (11 U.S.C. 707(b)) screens on income (6-month average vs. Vermont median), not DTI. So a Vermont household with 80% DTI but below-median income still qualifies for Chapter 7; a below-median DTI with above-median income might be pushed into Chapter 13.

The Vermont median-income thresholds are updated semi-annually by the UST. See means test explainer.

Related Vermont Resources

Bankruptcy means test explainer

DTI calculator

Front vs. back-end DTI

Vermont avg CC debt

Vermont credit card forgiveness
